nodes.name: New Task Form Submission
nodes.notes: Serves an n8n-hosted form (Title, Assignee, Duedate). Each submission becomes one execution.

nodes.name: Stamp & Shape Task
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes taskId, receivedAt. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Payload Valid?
nodes.notes: Two-way gate on ={{ $json.taskId }}. TRUE continues the happy path, FALSE takes the alternate branch. Watch out: The false branch carries the non-matching items — wire it deliberately rather than leaving it dangling.

nodes.name: Record Rejected Input
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'tracking sheet' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Route by Work Type
nodes.notes: Routes each item to one of 3 lanes: auto-approve, needs-review + fallback. Watch out: Unmatched items go to the fallback output; without one they are silently dropped.

nodes.name: Delegate 'auto-approve' to Sub-workflow
nodes.notes: Delegates to a reusable sub-workflow (single-responsibility building block) and waits for its result. Watch out: The sub-workflow needs an Execute Sub-workflow Trigger as its entry point. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run.

nodes.name: Fast-Track 'needs-review' + Alert
nodes.notes: Posts a message to Slack (#projects) — a low-latency way for the team to see automation activity without checking a dashboard. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Slack OAuth2. Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.

nodes.name: Hold Unknown Types (DLQ)
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Task Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Merge Routed Work
nodes.notes: Rejoins 3 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Stamp Completion Time
nodes.notes: Stamps completedAt with the current time for auditing.

nodes.name: Persist Run Metadata
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Load Previous Snapshot
nodes.notes: Reads every row from 'Task Tracker' — the read side of the store, e.g. for a digest or a downstream sync. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Compute Drift vs Snapshot
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Compare current metrics with the previous snapshot Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Enrich with Reference Data
nodes.notes: GET https://enrichment.example.com/v2/lookup — retries 3× with backoff on failure. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: API key / bearer for the target API. Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.

nodes.name: Fold In Enrichment Fields
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes enrichedAt, enrichmentSource. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
nodes.notes: Delegates to a reusable sub-workflow (single-responsibility building block) and waits for its result. Watch out: The sub-workflow needs an Execute Sub-workflow Trigger as its entry point. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run.

nodes.name: Record Sub-workflow Result
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Serialize Run Output (CSV)
nodes.notes: Serializes items to a CSV binary file.

nodes.name: Archive Copy to Google Drive
nodes.notes: Uploads the generated file to Google Drive as a timestamped archive copy. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2. Google Cloud Console → enable Drive API → OAuth2 client or Service Account.

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build a stable idempotency key per task (djb2 hash, no deps) Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Drop Already-Processed Items
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.name: Tag Pipeline Metadata
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes pipeline, version. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Stamp Processing Time
nodes.notes: Stamps processedAt with the current time for auditing.

nodes.name: Cap Batch Volume
nodes.notes: Caps the stream at 25 items to protect downstream quotas.

nodes.name: Align Field Names
nodes.notes: Normalizes field names so every source feeds the same downstream schema.

nodes.name: Sort Tasks Newest First
nodes.notes: Orders items (newest first) so limits and digests pick the most relevant records.

nodes.name: Summarize Run Stats
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes runAt, itemCount, status. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Append Audit Row (Notion)
nodes.notes: Creates a new page in the Notion database — the title is pulled straight from the item's key field. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Notion integration token. notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.

# Review expenses: Google Sheets

**Pattern:** Approval Workflow · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Form

## Overview

Starts when the form is submitted, and covers onboarding work end to end across Google Sheets, Notion, Outlook, Slack and Google Drive.

It moves through 29 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. New Task Form Submission
2. Stamp & Shape Task
3. Payload Valid?
4. Record Rejected Input
5. Route by Work Type
6. Delegate 'auto-approve' to Sub-workflow
7. Fast-Track 'needs-review' + Alert
8. Hold Unknown Types (DLQ)
9. Merge Routed Work
10. Stamp Completion Time
11. Persist Run Metadata
12. Load Previous Snapshot
13. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
14. Enrich with Reference Data
15. Fold In Enrichment Fields
16. Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
17. Record Sub-workflow Result
18. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
19. Archive Copy to Google Drive
20. Fingerprint for Idempotency
21. Drop Already-Processed Items
22. Tag Pipeline Metadata
23. Stamp Processing Time
24. Cap Batch Volume
25. Align Field Names
26. Sort Tasks Newest First
27. Summarize Run Stats
28. Append Audit Row (Notion)
29. Send Summary to Outlook

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Outlook → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing onboarding work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

New Task Form Submission → Stamp & Shape Task → Payload Valid? → Record Rejected Input → Route by Work Type → Delegate 'auto-approve' to Sub-workflow → Fast-Track 'needs-review' + Alert → Hold Unknown Types (DLQ) → Merge Routed Work → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow → Record Sub-workflow Result → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Copy to Google Drive → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Stamp Processing Time → Cap Batch Volume → Align Field Names → Sort Tasks Newest First → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Notion) → Send Summary to Outlook → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Outlook → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and Notion aligned by hand for onboarding
- Intake checked for completeness before it is stored in Google Sheets, for onboarding
- Onboarding work where "Stamp & Shape Task" is still a manual step before Google Sheets
- Onboarding work that only reaches Google Sheets when a form is submitted, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and Notion in step for onboarding, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Google Sheets or Notion are skipped, across all 32 nodes of this onboarding build
- A failed Google Sheets or Notion call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 32 nodes in this onboarding build
- Branches rejoin before Google Sheets, so a onboarding run reports once rather than 32 times
- Every onboarding run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Google Sheets

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Google OAuth2; Google OAuth2 / service account; Microsoft OAuth2; Notion integration token; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Unrecognized work types are parked in a dead-letter lane instead of erroring the whole run or silently dropping the item — new event kinds will show up eventually, and this is where you'd notice one without losing it. One kind is deliberately routed through a sub-workflow to show how heavier per-type logic can be extracted without touching this router at all.

## Practice exercises

About as deep as this pattern goes — extend it:

1. Send a work-type value that matches no switch rule and confirm it lands in the dead-letter branch.
2. Add a new work type and its own handling branch.
3. Replace the direct-write branch with a sub-workflow call, matching the pattern already used for the first kind.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Google OAuth2**
Google Cloud Console → enable Drive API → OAuth2 client or Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Service Accounts have their own empty Drive — share the target folder with it.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

**Microsoft OAuth2**
Azure Portal → App registrations → Microsoft Graph → Mail.Send / Mail.Read.
_Gotcha:_ Choose delegated vs application permissions deliberately; they behave differently.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your onboarding process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.
- Outlook: use `Mail.Send` alone if nothing here reads the mailbox.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole onboarding payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
